description: Comparative terrain, solar, and thermal metrics between lunar polar sites and primary terrestrial analog sites.

sites.name: Mauna Kea Summit / Saddle (Hawaii, USA)

solar_access.cloud_attenuation_note: High-altitude clear atmosphere with periodic orographic cloud cover.

sites.primary_analog_use: Rover mobility, wheel-soil shear testing, lunar soil simulant geotechnical evaluation.
sites.citation: Hamilton, V. E. et al. (2020), Field Characterization of Lunar Regolith Analogs at Mauna Kea, Planetary and Space Science.

sites.name: Antarctic Plateau (Concordia Station / Dome C)

solar_access.note: Continuous low-elevation solar illumination (10°-30°) during austral summer; total darkness during winter.

sites.primary_analog_use: Extreme cold survival, low-sun-angle solar arrays, psychological astronaut isolation.
sites.citation: Genthon, C. et al. (2010), Meteorological and surface heat-flux properties at Dome C, Antarctica, J. Geophys. Res.

sites.name: Atacama Desert (Yungay / Valle de la Luna, Chile)

solar_access.note: World-leading direct normal solar irradiance; >90% cloud-free days.

sites.primary_analog_use: Dust abrasion, solar panel dust accumulation, extreme desiccation testing.
sites.citation: McKay, C. P. et al. (2003), Temperature and Moisture Conditions for Life in the Extreme Arid Core of the Atacama Desert, Astrobiology.
